literature_notes: Three ledger lines were evaluated (L1, L2, L3), all from the same PMC source (PMC12894981). L1 describes a GFP-tagged MCT2-embigin fusion construct: this is a chimeric protein of two proteins, and the clip does not state on which protein's terminus the GFP sits, nor any residue number — the tag position on embigin specifically is indeterminate. L2 describes 'RFP tagged embigin' with no specification of N-terminal vs C-terminal placement; embigin is a type I single-pass protein with an extracellular N-terminus (mature residue 33, after SP cleavage at 32) and an intracellular C-terminus (residue 327), so both termini exist and neither is ruled out by the clip alone. The topology_derived rule requires that the clip establish a tag at a terminus AND that exactly one terminus is extracellular — the first condition is not met because the clip is silent on which terminus carries the RFP. Applying topology_derived here would require structural inference (that researchers would naturally tag the extracellular face), which is explicitly forbidden. L3 describes a confocal microscopy assay for expression and localization of MCT1-embigin fusion and embigin constructs but names no tag, no residue, and no terminus. No clip names a residue, a terminus, or an extracellular face for any tag on embigin; therefore zero sites qualify.
